entities.summary: Carl Emil Seashore, born Sjöstrand was a prominent American psychologist and educator. He was the author of numerous books and articles principally regarding the fields of speech–language pathology, music education, and the psychology of music and art. He served as Dean of the Graduate College of University of Iowa from 1908–1937. He is most commonly associated with the development of the Seashore Tests of Musical Ability. Carl Seashore was a physicians & medical pioneers from Mörlunda (1866-01-28, Mörlunda–1949-10-16). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Carl Seashore's work on music education and the Seashore Tests of Musical Ability had a significant impact on the field of music therapy, with his tests being used to assess musical ability in over 200,000 individuals. His contributions also influenced the development of music education programs in schools across North America.
